 :JUDGMENT:
The Petitioners in M.V.C. No.2033/2020 and MVC.2034/2020 have filed the Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs. 10,00,000/
and Rs. 30,00,000/ respectively for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Since both these Petitions arise out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 2312 2021 in MVC No.2033/2020, these two cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 26082019 at about 9.15 a.m. the Petitioners were proceeding in a Scooter bearing No.KA01EV2548 near Command hospital, Old Air Port road, at that time, a car bearing No.KA50M 3808 was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Scooter of the Petitioners.
Due to the said impact, both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.2033/2020 was shifted to Manipal Hospital wherein she took conservative line treatment and outpatient basis.
Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.2034/2020 was shifted to Manipal Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.2033/2020 was hale and healthy and she was a housewife.

Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
2
5. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.No.2034/2020 was hale and healthy and was working as a Driver and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.

6. The Petitioners of both the Petitions have contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA50M3808 which is owned by the Respondent No.1 and insured with Respondent No.2.
As such, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
7. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents in both petitions, both the Respondents appeared before the Court through their counsels and filed their detailed separate Objection Statement.
8. In both the petitions, Respondent No.1 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners.
Further he denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
This respondent has admitted that he is the owner of the alleged offending car and the same was duly insured with the 2nd respondent and the same is in force as on the date of the accident.

Further he has contended that the driver of the car drove the vehicle in a moderate speed, but the rider of the scooter rode his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner without following any of the traffic rules and regulations and all of a sudden stopped the vehicle without giving indication and caused the accident.
On these grounds, he has prayed to dismiss both the petitions.
In both the petitions, Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners.
Further it denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of alleged offending car and it was valid as on the date of alleged accident, but its liability is subject to terms and conditions enumerated in the policy.

Further it contended that the driver of the car was not possessing valid and effective driving license, hence the investigating officer after thorough investigation filed charge sheet under section 3(1) and 181 of IMV Act.

Further contended that the owner of the car knowing fully that the driver did not possess valid driving licence has entrusted the said vehicle to him and has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in both the petitions and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioners.
Further it contended that the rider of the Motorcycle did not possess valid driving license.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss both the petitions.
9. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
ISSUES IN MVC No.2033/2020 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 26.08.2019 at about 9.15 a.m. near Command hospital, Old Airport road, Halasur,
Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA 50M 3808?

Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
3 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
ISSUES IN MVC No.2034/2020 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 26.08.2019 at about 9.15 a.m. near Command hospital, Old Airport road, Halasur,
Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA 04 MW6914?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner in MVC.2033/2020 got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.

The Petitioner in MVC.2034/2020 got examined his wife/next friend and guardian as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P11to Ex.P18 and examined one witness as PW.3 on his behalf and got marked documents as per Ex.P.19 and P20 and closed their side evidence.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has examined the Superintendent at RTO office, Yelahanka as RW.1 and its official as RW.2 and got marked 5 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5 and closed its side.

11. The Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has relied on the decisions reported as under;
1. AIR 2004 (3) SCC 343 Hon'ble Supreme Court between Malla Prakasa Rao Vs. Malla Janaki and others 2.AIR 2020 SC 4453 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India between Beli Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and another.

I have perused the citations relied by the respondent No.2, depositions,
documents exhibited and materials available on record.

13. My answer to the Issues in MVC.2033/2020 are as under:
 Issue No. 1 : In the Affirmative Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/

14. My answer to the Issues in MVC No.2034/2020 are as under:
 Issue No. 1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

16. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, the Petitioner in MVC.2033/2020 got examined herself as P.W.1 and the Petitioner in MVC.2034/2020 got examined his wife/next friend and guardian as P.W.2 and one witness got examined as PW.3.
They got marked in total 20 documents.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the True copies of FIR along with Complaint, Spot Panchanama along with sketch map, IMV report, Notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Reply to the Notice, Wound Certificate, Charge Sheet and statement of eyewitness.

17. Upon going through the police documents, it shows that on the complaint lodged by one Kala M./petitioner in MVC 2033/2020, the case was registered against the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA50M3808 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P2 is the Spot Panchanama along with sketch map which shows that the concerned police had drawn the Spot Panchanama at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P3 is the IMV Report wherein the Motor Vehicle Inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is the Notice u/s 133 of MV Act and Ex.P.5 is the Reply to the notice.
Ex.P6 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner in MVC.2033/2020.

Ex.P7 is the True copy of Charge sheet shows that the driver of car bearing No. KA50M3808 was charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338, 3(1) of IPC r/w Section 181 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.11 is the wound certificate of the Petitioner in MVC No.2024/2020 18.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1 and PW.2 in length.
In the crossexamination both PW.1 and PW.2 have denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioners.

19. Though the Respondent No.2 had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, it did not produced any documents Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
5 or evidence to substantiate its contentions.

entities.text: Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Chargesheet against the driver of the offending car.

20. The oral and documentary evidence of P.W.1 and PW.2 and the materials available on record,
clearly shows that the said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and Petitioners in both the cases had sustained injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in both the cases in the "Affirmative".
21. Issue No. 2 in MVC.2033/2020 : As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
22. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 52 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.9 to prove her age.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 22.07.1967.
The accident took place on 26.08.2019.
Hence, the age of the petitioner 52 years is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
23. It is to be noted here that, according to the petitioner, she had sustained grievous injuries.

But,
the medical record produced by the Petitioner herself, i.e., Ex.P.6 Wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. 3x3 cm abrasion over right elbow 2. Contusion back with pain
The Doctor has opined that Injuries are simple in nature.
As admitted by the petitioner in her crossexamination that she has not admitted as inpatient in the hospital as her injuries are simple in nature.
24. In order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce documents.
But, the documents produced by the Petitioner shows that she had sustained simple injuries.

The petitioner has produced the medical bill, i.e., Ex.P10 shows the total medical bills are amounting to Rs.4,800/.
25.
It is not the case of the Petitioner that she has suffered from any permanent disability.
Admittedly, the Petitioner is aged about 52 years.

In the absence of fracture or other physical disability and considering the simple injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for medical expenses, pain and sufferings, food and nourishment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/ would be just and proper.
26. Issue No. 2 in MVC No. 2034/2020 :
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
6 27.
In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 55 years.
The Petitioner has produced Driving licence at Ex.P12 to prove his age.
As per Driving licence, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 10071962.
The accident took place on 26.08.2019.
Hence, the age of the petitioner 57 years is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.

28. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was working as Driver and was earning Rs.20,000/
per month.
In this regard, except driving licence he has not produced any supportive documents to show that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was working as driver.

Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2019, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
29. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
30.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P11 and other medical records reveal that in the accident the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
Traumatic brain injury with SAH, SDH multiple facial injury, fracture of right hemiplegia.
In the wound certificate the Doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
However, the doctor has not been examined in this case.
31. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
32.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
33.
The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 26082019 and discharged on 23092019 in Manipal hospital.
Upon going through Ex.P20 i.e., the inpatient record show that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 26082019 and discharged on 23092019 in Manipal hospital.
i.e., for nearly one month.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is one month.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.42,000/ under this head (@ Rs.14,000/ per month ).
Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
7
IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

34. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.9,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day for 90 days) towards attendants charges,
Rs.9,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.9,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.27,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
35. The PW.2 has deposed that he has spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
He has produced 23 medical bills at Ex.P.14.
I have gone through the medical bills and I found that the petitioner has got benefit of Mediclaim policy.
The medical bills produced reflects that they are the approximate bills.
Apart from that, no supportive documents are furnished to show that the petitioner herein has paid said medical bills out of his pocket.
Apart from that, if the cross examination done in respect of the medical bills are taken into consideration, there is no serious dispute regarding the medical bills.
However, the medical bills clearly reflects regarding reimbursement of sum of Rs.3,80,000/ from the Medi Assist India Pvt. Ltd.
And it also reflects the patient has paid sum of Rs.5,60,221/.
There is also admission during crossexamination regarding the fact that there is reimbursement from Medi Assit India Pvt. Ltd.
Under these circumstances, this tribunal is of the view the petitioner is entitled for medical bills to the tune of Rs.6,01,511/ only  .which is rounded off to Rs.6,01,600/ .
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs. 6,01,600/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
36. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is unable to carry out his day to day activities.

37. Further, the PW.2 has produced Neurophysiological assessment report, Initial assessment and discharge summary of Manipal hospital, Radiological report, speech and language evaluation report at Ex.P.15 to 18, in addition to this Petitioner has also got examined Smt. Padma T., Senior Team Member in Medical Records Department of Manipal hospital as PW.3 who has produced Authorization letter, 4 Inpatient records at Ex.P.19.

sentences.text: But the petitioner has not examined the doctor regarding the permanent disability.
Hence this tribunal is of the view that there being any evidence of the competent witness this tribunal cannot assess the disability of the petitioner on its own.
Accordingly, tribunal is in of view that the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation for future disability.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 27,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 6,01,600/
5.

Loss of income during the laid Rs. 42,000/ up period Total Rs. 7,60,600/
39.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.7,60,600/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

40. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA50M3808.
It is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that on the alleged date, the driver of the offending car had driven the same without having valid and effective Driving licence.

In order to prove the said contention, the Respondent No.2 examined the Superintendent, RTO, Yelahanka as RW.1 who has produced DL extract of 1st respondent at Ex.R.1 which is valid from 16.09.2019 to 15.09.2024.
The document speak for itself that as on the date of accident the DL of the driver of the car was not effective.
Though the same was renewed subsequently, it will not come to the aid of the owner/driver which will support the contentions raised by the insurance company.
The witness who got examined on behalf of the company also deposed the said fact.

Further the 2nd respondent has also examined its Legal Manager as RW.2 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R.2 to R.5 i.e.,
Authorization letter, Certified copy of policy, copy of notice and postal receipt as Ex.R.5.
All these documents show that the 1st respondent was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
In this regard the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet under Section 3(1) 181 of MV Act.
This fact is justified from the document Ex.P.7 charge sheet.
During cross examination of RW.1 and 2 suggestions are made to contradict the evidence given by RW.1 and 2.
However, RW.1 and 2 withstood during their cross examination to the averments deposed by them during their examination in chief.

41. From the careful consideration of the documentary evidence available on record, it is evident that the police concerned/IO has submitted charge sheet against Sudharshan and in the charge sheet submitted to the Court, the respondent No.1 is shown as accused No.1 and he is alleged of offences punishable u/sections 279, 337, 338, 3(1) of IPC r/w Sec. 181 of IMV Act.

Such being the case, when the documents speak for itself regarding the fact that driver had no DL to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident, certainly the driver is to be held liable to pay compensation.

Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
9 42.
Now, coming to the decisions relied upon by the petitioners in support of their case as noted above, I have given careful reading to all the decisions.

The facts and circumstances which arisen in those decisions before the respective Hon'ble Courts differs to that of the facts and circumstances of the case on hand as in the present case the issue is regarding the fact that as on the date of accident,
the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence.
Whereas in the cases before the Hon'ble Courts, the issue was regarding possession of fake driving licence by the rider of the vehicle.

Apart from that, the facts and circumstances of the case before the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision AIR 2018 SC 2662 differs to the facts and circumstances of the case on hand as before the Hon'ble Apex Court the issue was regarding the fact that offending vehicle had no permit to ply on the road.
Whereas same is not the question involved in the case on hand.
Hence, with great respect, this Tribunal is of the view that the decisions relied upon by the petitioners will not come to their aid.

43. In MFA No.3297/2019 at para No.28 of the judgment, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that; "Learned counsel for the insurance company further placed reliance on the judgments of the Apex Court reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531(National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh and others) and (2018) 3 SCC 208 (Pappu and others Vs.Vinod Kumar Lamba and another).

entities.text: AIR 2004 SC 1531(National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: (2018) 3 SCC 208 (Pappu and others Vs.Vinod Kumar Lamba and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court in Swaran Singh's case referred above has clearly held that, mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence at relevant timeNot in themselves available defences for insurance company under Section 149(2) (a) (ii) of MV Act.

It is further observed that the rider of the vehicle admittedly did not possess any driving licence and the owner consciously let him to ride the vehicle and in such circumstances, the insurer is entitled to succeed in its defence and avoid liability.

In para No.105 of the said judgment, the Larger Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme court has laid down the guidelines as to under what circumstances, the insurance company can raise defences under Section 149(2)(a)
(ii) of the MV Act and instances were quoted.

In view of these guidelines, it is evident that non possessing driving licence is a valid ground for the insurance company to succeed and in the instant case, the rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.
These observations were again reiterated by the Apex Court in Pappu's case referred supra and they were reproduced in para No.18.

Considering the said aspects, it is evident that the respondent No.1/owner, who consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence, cannot take the benefit of his own wrong, and the insurance company is entitled to raise a defence under Section 149(2) of MV Act.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on respondent No.1/owner himself.
The Tribunal considering the evidence on record has rightly fastened the liability to respondent No.1/owner, which does not call for any interference.

44. In the decision MFA.7404/2014 decided on 6 th December 2022, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held the same principles which is held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.3297/2019.

In the light of principles held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka if careful consideration is given to the documents Ex.P7 i.e., charge sheet filed against the respondent No.1 who is also the driver of the car in question, it is clear that there is breach of policy conditions by the owner cum driver of car as he had driven the same without possessing valid and effective driving Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
10 licence to drive the car as on the date of accident.

Moreover, record reveals that though respondent No.1 has contested the petition, nothing has been brought before this court to substantiate the contentions taken up in the statement of objections filed.

Such being the case, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay compensation and in other words it can be held that the owner/respondent No.1 shall be held liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The theory or principle of pay and recovery cannot be applied to t76he case on hand.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
45. Issue No.3 in both cases : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC.2033/2020 against the Respondents No. 1 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC No.2034/2020 against the Respondent No. 1 under Sec. 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.2033/2020  is entitled for Global compensation of  Rs.50,000/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.2034/2020 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,60,600/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
Petitions against Respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 3 months from the date of this award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner in MVC.2034/2020, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.
Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
11

On deposit of the Award amount and  interest by the Respondent No.1 in  MVC.2033/2020, since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E Payment after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ respectively in both cases.
Draw Award accordingly.
Keep the Original Judgment in  MVC.2033/2020 and the copy of the  Judgment in M.V.C. No.2034/2020.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and Petitioners in both the cases had sustained injuries.
Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2019, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
Hence this tribunal is of the view that there being any evidence of the competent witness this tribunal cannot assess the disability of the petitioner on its own.
Accordingly, tribunal is in of view that the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation for future disability.
All these documents show that the 1st respondent was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
In this regard the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet under Section 3(1) 181 of MV Act.
Such being the case, when the documents speak for itself regarding the fact that driver had no DL to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident, certainly the driver is to be held liable to pay compensation.
The facts and circumstances which arisen in those decisions before the respective Hon'ble Courts differs to that of the facts and circumstances of the case on hand as in the present case the issue is regarding the fact that as on the date of accident,
the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence.
Whereas in the cases before the Hon'ble Courts, the issue was regarding possession of fake driving licence by the rider of the vehicle.
Apart from that, the facts and circumstances of the case before the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision AIR 2018 SC 2662 differs to the facts and circumstances of the case on hand as before the Hon'ble Apex Court the issue was regarding the fact that offending vehicle had no permit to ply on the road.
Whereas same is not the question involved in the case on hand.
Hence, with great respect, this Tribunal is of the view that the decisions relied upon by the petitioners will not come to their aid.
In view of these guidelines, it is evident that non possessing driving licence is a valid ground for the insurance company to succeed and in the instant case, the rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.
Considering the said aspects, it is evident that the respondent No.1/owner, who consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence, cannot take the benefit of his own wrong, and the insurance company is entitled to raise a defence under Section 149(2) of MV Act.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on respondent No.1/owner himself.
The Tribunal considering the evidence on record has rightly fastened the liability to respondent No.1/owner, which does not call for any interference.
In the light of principles held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka if careful consideration is given to the documents Ex.P7 i.e., charge sheet filed against the respondent No.1 who is also the driver of the car in question, it is clear that there is breach of policy conditions by the owner cum driver of car as he had driven the same without possessing valid and effective driving Kala M vs S.Sudarshanan on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139359492/
10 licence to drive the car as on the date of accident.
Moreover, record reveals that though respondent No.1 has contested the petition, nothing has been brought before this court to substantiate the contentions taken up in the statement of objections filed.
Such being the case, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay compensation and in other words it can be held that the owner/respondent No.1 shall be held liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The theory or principle of pay and recovery cannot be applied to t76he case on hand.
